answer: A Sybil-resistant agent economy can require every identity to sit as a vertex in a stake-bonded trust graph: joining costs a refundable bond, and each vertex needs vouches from established agents who lose part of their own bond if the newcomer misbehaves. A haven of honest agents therefore stays expensive to infiltrate, since each fake identity needs fresh stake plus trusted sponsors, while the nectar of shared rewards flows only to vertices with real history. Attack cost grows linearly with each fake, so mass forgery stops paying.
